best_signals: RSI 55-60 at entry: 2/2 wins (100%), avg +2.15% -- the ONLY consistently profitable bucket for the LEGACY intraday RSI strategy; n=2, thin sample, INFORMATIONAL ONLY now that the live strategy is MA-20/60 trend-following. Do not act on it without n>=10.

Single shallow-cross probation entries (heavy size-DOWN, NOT skip) -- verdict POSITIVE and durable. BMY (0.13% cross, 50% unit) is the book's premier anchor at +9.91% Day 32. GIS (0.29% cross, 75% unit) at +6.04% Day 34. CAG (0.113% cross, 50% unit) at +4.40% Day 21, comfortable cushion ~10.9%. Read: the discipline keeps validating; size down on a single clean shallow cross, do not upsize, weight the entry's SECTOR trend.

Defensive/quality tilt is a REGIME-CONDITIONAL edge that beats on down/flat tapes by holding value and keeps pace on up-days ONLY when its financials/tech leaders (SCHW, CRM, MSFT) participate; it lags up-days led by names Bull does not own. NOTE the limit exposed today: the defensive book cushions broad market weakness but does NOT protect against an idiosyncratic single-name stop-out -- AMZN's -6.57% fill alone turned a roughly market-matching day into a -0.58% miss. The edge is portfolio-level and tape-conditional, not a guarantee on any given session.
avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) -- CONFIRMED LOSER, thesis now RESOLVED by AMZN. AMZN (entered Aug 4 at +15.2% above EMA20, the book's most-extended admit) was the lone red hold for two weeks and stopped out today at -6.57% (-$619.82), exactly as the extension-loser rule predicted (prior confirm: META Jul 15 at ~8.5% ext, stopped -8.04% Jul 23). The other extended admits are the SPLIT survivors: MSFT (Aug 3, +15.5% ext) now -1.07% but holding (cushion 5.01%), CRM (Aug 4, +7.2% ext) at +2.99% (cushion 11.6%), QQQ (Aug 5, +3.5% mild ext) at +0.46% (cushion 4.71%). Net read: heavily-extended tech is a coin-flip that skews to the downside -- the worst-extended (AMZN) died, the rest hold thin. Firm rule stands: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross (PDBC), SKIP outright. MSFT is now the extended-admit-under-pressure watch (red, thinning cushion) in AMZN's place.

STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- RESOLVED as a SKIP, not a size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6.05% extended + thin liq, quarter-unit Jul 24) stopped out -2.40% Day 3. Distinguish from a SINGLE shallow-cross flag (BMY/GIS/CAG), a valid size-DOWN. Rule: one flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. CRM (Aug 4) carried TWO soft flags (0.34% cross + 7.2% extended) but no thin-liq strike; taken via notional cap -- now +2.99% by Day 13, so the two-soft-flag boundary test still reads POSITIVE. Keep the one-flag-size-down / two-flag-skip rule as is.

Shallow EMA cross entries on earnings-adjacent names: TSLA (Jul 7, 0.06% cross, earnings Jul 22) lost -4.78%. Rule: SKIP (do not size down) when BOTH shallow cross (<0.5%) AND earnings within 14 days. Re-validated Jul 30 (OXY skipped).

BMY at 0.13% and CAG at 0.113% cleared this line at half unit and validated. 0.1% remains the skip floor. NOTE: a cross below the floor at one snapshot can MATURE -- QQQ's cross widened 0.013%->0.224% intraday and was taken; NVDA's 0.07% flag matured to 0.350% by the Aug 5 scan. Re-check on the next scan rather than permanently blacklisting.

Earnings-blackout holds ride to the hard stop with no discretionary exit: CMG (Jul 10 entry, blackout Jul 15-29) drifted to its 2xATR stop and filled at -8.06% Jul 22. Blackout policy working as intended -- record of realized blackout downside, not a rule change.

Grotesquely-extended/parabolic golden crosses -- SMCI (Aug 13-14 scan): WIDE decisive cross (+1.42% spread) but +25.7% above EMA20 (worst the book has ever scanned) with a hot 6.7% ATR. Prime chase/reversal risk; treat as size-DOWN/wait-for-pullback per the extended-loser rule even when the cross itself is clean. Skipped both scans.

LEGACY intraday RSI buckets (informational, strategy retired): RSI 60-65 0/3, RSI 65-75 0/1, gap-up opens with RSI>60 -- all losers historically. Retained only as a record of why the intraday RSI approach was abandoned for trend-following.
